To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) STDP based learning algorithms are limited to shallow SNN architectures and (ii) spike based error back propagation can be effectively used for training deeper SNNs for energy efficient inference

(i) STDP based learning can be harnassed for unsupervised feature learning in SNN but is limited in applicabilty to shallow SNN, (ii) ANN to SNN can be used to scale the SANN to deeper layers and achieve state of the art accuracies but at the cost of high inference latency and (iii) Spike based error backpropogation can be used to minimize inference latency of ANN to SNN converted networks while yielding comparable accuracy

(1) STDP based learning enables SNNs to achieve 70.1% accuracy on CIFAR 100 with 1.6M training samples, (2) ANN to SNN conversions enable SNN to achieve 69.96 % accuracy on ImageNet, and (3) Spike based backpropagation reduces the inference latency of ANN to SNN converted networks by 8x.
